onboarding.theme: Roadmap/unavailable content on the sign-in screen makes the front door feel like a construction site
onboarding.quote: I would move all the roadmap and 'not yet available' content off the sign-in card; the front door should feel finished, not like a construction site.
onboarding.change: Remove the SSO/SCIM/SIEM 'Planned' teasers and the roadmap card from the sign-in and MFA screens entirely; relocate all forward-looking items to a single collapsed 'Roadmap' section on the Account page, so the login card shows only functioning fields.

onboarding.theme: Literal unresolved '[quarter]' / '[code]' placeholders read as broken and undercut credibility
onboarding.quote: the visible '[quarter]' placeholder undercuts it further... replace the bracketed placeholder text with a real date or drop the SSO teaser from the sign-in card entirely.
onboarding.change: Replace every literal '[quarter]' and '[code]' token in the roadmap/SSO labels and reset flow with a real ISO target date (e.g. '2026-Q4') pulled from config, or delete the label; add a build-time lint that fails on any unresolved '[...]' placeholder in shipped copy.

onboarding.theme: SSO/SAML/OIDC + SCIM being roadmap-only is a hard enterprise adoption gate
onboarding.quote: no enterprise regulatory team rolls this to nine-plus users on per-workspace passwords, so those are table stakes, not nice-to-haves.
onboarding.change: Ship SAML/OIDC SSO and SCIM provisioning as a first release feature (not roadmap), gated per-workspace in the Account > Security page, and make MFA required-by-default for regulatory workspaces rather than an optional per-account toggle.

onboarding.theme: Enterprise/crypto acronym soup (TOTP, SSO, SCIM, SIEM, otpauth URI, HttpOnly) with no plain-language gloss
onboarding.quote: 'TOTP MFA,' 'SSO (SAML/OIDC),' 'SCIM,' 'SIEM' and 'HttpOnly cookie' are alphabet soup to me — I'd have no idea what half of those do without asking someone younger.
onboarding.change: Add an inline hover/tooltip gloss on first mention of every acronym (MFA, TOTP, SSO, SCIM, SIEM, otpauth URI) the same way roles are glossed, and move HttpOnly/salted-hash/audit-stream crypto detail behind a 'For your IT department' expander so the sign-in card stays plain.

onboarding.theme: Trust needs proof, not prose: exportable, tamper-evident audit log + validated self-hosted/residency + real vs demo
onboarding.quote: I'd need a validated self-hosted install with real reset email and documented audit evidence before staking a Health Canada sequence on it.
onboarding.change: Add an audit-log viewer on the Account page that shows retention period, states it is tamper-evident/append-only, survives workspace deletion, captures operational events (who ran validation, who transmitted), and offers a dated exportable trail (PDF/CSV); surface the 'Deployment & data residency' (self-hosted) statement on the first sign-in screen and provide a real reset email path outside demo mode.

onboarding.theme: 'Workspace' is used constantly but never defined, and admin role names (workspace-admin/tenant-admin/owner) blur together
onboarding.quote: 'workspace' is used a dozen times but never defined for a first-timer — one sentence saying what a workspace actually maps to would help.
onboarding.change: Add a one-line 'What is a workspace?' tooltip on the first isolation line at signup (workspace = one isolated client company's dossiers), and add a disambiguating gloss on the role expander distinguishing owner vs tenant-admin vs workspace-admin so they cannot be conflated.

onboarding.theme: PMs/multi-client users want project visibility and a client/workspace switcher, not an all-identity onboarding
onboarding.quote: the whole onboarding is identity and security with zero hint of project visibility; I'd want the first screen after sign-in to surface deadlines, submission status, and who's blocked.
onboarding.change: Make the first post-sign-in screen a portfolio/status view (deadlines, submission status, who's blocked) with 'Guided journey' and 'Portfolio' prominent, and add a client/workspace switcher usable from a single identity so CRO/CDMO users move between clients without re-authenticating.

journey.theme: No visible validation engine, ruleset name, or version behind READY-TO-FILE
journey.quote: I'd need to see the actual eCTD validation engine, the Health Canada validation criteria version it's built against, and proof the checklist mapping stays current with each Health Canada guidance update before I'd stake a client's sequence on it.
journey.change: On the Readiness panel, replace the generic BLOCKED/READY light with an eValidator-style report: name and version-stamp the Health Canada validation ruleset (e.g. 'HC eCTD Validation Criteria vX.Y'), and list per-leaf rule IDs, severities, and pass/fail so the READY-TO-FILE badge is backed by a nameable, versioned rule set.

journey.theme: Dense, roadmap-heavy screens with 3D 'submission tower' defaulting on (round-5 regression)
journey.quote: there's an awful lot on this screen — a top bar with five chips, a left rail of ten steps, a center card, a right panel with a 3D tower, toggles, banners. My eyes don't know where to rest and I'd be nervous clicking anything for fear of setting something off.
journey.change: Make the plain printable Checklist table the default view and demote the 3D 'submission tower' to an opt-in toggle; collapse the transmission/lifecycle side panels behind progressive-disclosure so a single step (esp. Step 1 and Transmission) shows one thing at a time instead of tiles, panels, and banners at once.

journey.theme: No audit trail, Part-11 e-signature, data-residency or per-client isolation story
journey.quote: where is the audit trail, is the e-signature a Part-11-style controlled signature with an identity binding, and what happens to my dossier data in the cloud.
journey.change: Add an explicit Controls/Compliance panel on the QA and e-signature steps showing a tamper-evident audit trail (who-signed-what-when with identity binding), version locking, exportable audit log, plus stated data residency/retention and per-sponsor data isolation for multi-client CDMO/CRO users.

journey.theme: Regulatory claims (service-standard day counts, deficiency windows, Module 4 rule) not cited, dated, or wired to live calendar dates
journey.quote: let me see the deficiency-window logic (SDN 45, NOD 90/45-for-DIN, NON) tied to live dates, not just displayed, since that's what my deadline trackers exist to catch. Also... tell me which Health Canada validation ruleset/version underpins 'READY TO FILE'.
journey.change: Behind each regulatory value (SDN 45 / NOD 90/45-for-DIN / NON windows, lead times, the Module 4 rule) show a source-guidance citation with a 'last verified against HC guidance' date stamp, and convert the deficiency windows from static text into computed calendar deadlines driven by the submission type and live receipt date.

journey.theme: Forced 10-step linearity with no jump-to-module or multi-dossier/portfolio view
journey.quote: a linear 10-step 'journey' doesn't map to how we actually work parallel modules across several products at once. I'd want to know how much I can jump around versus being forced down the rail.
journey.change: Add a jump-to-any-unlocked-module affordance plus an expert/dense mode that bypasses the tutorial voice, and a portfolio roll-up ('My dossiers') showing on-time/at-risk/late status across multiple sponsors, with owner-per-step and due-date columns for PM/coordinator roles.

journey.theme: Module 4 'not required for a generic ANDS' stated as a flat rule, not a qualified conditional
journey.quote: it says Module 4 is 'not required for a generic ANDS,' which is an overgeneralization — comparative bioavailability and certain data can land there, so I'd want that qualified.
journey.change: On the Checklist M1–M5 mapping, restate the Module 4 note as a pathway-set conditional (flag the comparative-bioavailability/biowaiver exceptions) with a link to the specific HC guidance and an override control so the tool doesn't silently decide scope.

journey.theme: Acronym wall (SDN/NOD/NON/DIN/REP/CESG/MDN/ACK) with only ephemeral hover tooltips
journey.quote: give the acronym-heavy transmission and Lifecycle panels a plain-language glossary or 'explain like it's my first filing' mode instead of only hover tooltips, since I'd lose those on a printout.
journey.change: Add a persistent, always-open glossary/'what is this?' panel defining each acronym on first use (matching the receipt-tile tooltips) and carry those definitions onto the exported/printed Checklist so juniors, founders, and newcomers keep them off-screen and in review.

catalog.theme: Placeholder "d" ID can leak into a real filing — reminder is too soft, not a hard block
catalog.quote: the placeholder ID starts with "d" and six digits, but real Health Canada IDs are a letter plus six or seven, so I'd worry an operator forgets to swap it and files a fake "d" number - I'd make that draft chip louder and block filing outright until it's real.
catalog.change: Convert the "validation reminds you before filing" behaviour into a hard gate: on the Validate/Export step, refuse export (block, not warn) whenever a dossier still carries a placeholder "d" ID, and add a portfolio-level count of dossiers still on draft IDs on the catalog header.

catalog.theme: Trust needs concrete evidence, not walkthrough claims: exportable audit trail, retention/purge policy, Canadian data residency, server-side workspace isolation
catalog.quote: I'd want to know if anything is ever truly purged and on what retention schedule... And I'd insist on knowing where the workspace data physically resides — Canadian data residency is a real question my auditors will ask.
catalog.change: Add an exportable audit trail (per-dossier "Export audit to PDF" button capturing who/when/reason with a defined timezone), plus a Compliance/Trust panel on the catalog stating data-residency location, the retention/purge schedule for archived dossiers, and that workspace isolation is enforced server-side.

catalog.theme: Tile grid doesn't scale — portfolio managers need a sortable/filterable table with owner, due date, sequence and last-modified, plus status export
catalog.quote: the tile grid won't scale for a portfolio of dozens of products — give me a sortable table with filters by status, submission type and deadline, and bulk actions... this is a project manager's landing page with no project-management signal — add a target file date, days-remaining or overdue flags, an owner/assignee per dossier, and last-activity.
catalog.change: Add a table/list view toggle to the catalog with sortable, filterable columns (status, submission type, sponsor/client, target file date, owner/assignee, last-modified, latest sequence number), overdue flags, bulk actions, and a one-click portfolio status export (CSV/PDF) for client reports.

catalog.theme: "CS-BE" and submission type are hardcoded/opaque — should be driven by the chosen submission type and spelled out, with a "which type am I?" helper
catalog.quote: don't hardcode "CS-BE" on every tile, drive it from the actual submission type; ... I'd want a visible sequence/lifecycle indicator on each tile.
catalog.change: Replace the hardcoded "CS-BE" meta chip with the submission type actually selected at creation, show a plain-language label on the tile (not just the abbreviation), and add a clickable "Which submission type am I?" explainer next to the submission-type field in the New dossier card.

catalog.theme: "3/5 modules" progress conflates "present" with "validated" and hides sequence/lifecycle state — misleads on filing readiness
catalog.quote: I'd want the progress chip ("3/5 modules") to distinguish "present" from "validated and complete", because a module existing is not the same as it passing, and that distinction is where filings actually fail.
catalog.change: On each tile, split the "3/5 modules" chip into a present-vs-validated indicator and add sequence number + lifecycle status (original / supplement / notifiable change); ensure any "Ready to file" status is derived from an actual validation pass, not module presence.

catalog.theme: ID-format rule shown only after submit and formats are inconsistently specified — draft "d"+6 vs stated "one letter + 6–7 digits"
catalog.quote: the ID pattern error only appears after I try, so I'd rather see the "one letter + 6–7 digits" rule shown next to the field up front... the placeholder is "e123456" (six digits) and generated placeholders use "d" plus six — I'd want the accepted formats spelled out against current HC conventions rather than a loose regex.
catalog.change: Show the accepted Dossier ID format inline beside the ID field before submit with live as-you-type validation, and explicitly spell out both accepted real formats and the reserved "d"-prefix draft format (verified against current HC/REP conventions) instead of a single loose regex.

catalog.theme: No bilingual (English/French) signalling — Module 1 monographs are dual-language and the whole UI must work in both official languages
catalog.quote: there's no mention of French anywhere, and as a bilingual specialist in Laval I need the whole interface, tooltips and product names to work in both official languages, not just English placeholders like "Drugazole 10 mg tablet".
catalog.change: Add a bilingual product-name field (EN/FR) and a language indicator on each tile at dossier creation, and surface which official languages a dossier's Module 1 content tracks.

builder_forms.theme: Screen too dense / overwhelming on first read
builder_forms.quote: Honestly, this looks dense. There's a three-column workspace, glyph legends, module tabs, right-rail cards, and a dozen chips before I've entered a single value... my first hour is spent learning the tool, not filing.
builder_forms.change: Add a 'Guided mode' default toggle on the builder that collapses the right rail, module tabs, and provenance/portfolio chips, and drives a single 'Next required section' focus view with one primary CTA per section; expose the full three-column expert view only via an explicit 'Show all controls' switch.

builder_forms.theme: Guidance/schema/profile versions not pinned to dated Health Canada releases
builder_forms.quote: state the exact schema/stylesheet version the XML PM validator checks against, with a visible 'last updated' date, because a French translator like me lives and dies by whether the tool matches the current Health Canada release.
builder_forms.change: On the 'What this does / does NOT check' expander and every 'Health Canada guidance ↗' link, show the specific guidance/eCTD validation profile + XML PM schema/stylesheet document number, version, and a 'reconciled against HC on <date>' timestamp; add the same version stamp to the XML PM validator card.

builder_forms.theme: Two inconsistent provenance/review mechanics (sample-ghost vs AI-draft confirm) confuse users
builder_forms.quote: the AI-draft path lets me self-attest 'this is my content' with a single button while the sample path won't let me confirm at all — inconsistent, and the self-attest button is a weak gate for AI-generated regulatory text; I'd want a diff showing what actually changed from the draft.
builder_forms.change: Consolidate the sample/ghost and AI-draft flows into one 'Provenance & review' control per field with a single consistent clearing rule, and make the AI-draft 'I have reviewed this — it is my content' confirm require viewing a diff of what changed before it can be clicked.

builder_forms.theme: No exportable, immutable audit trail / Part-11 e-signature evidence
builder_forms.quote: there's no mention of an audit log I can export, versioning of documents, or who authored/approved each change with a timestamp, and that's the first thing an inspector asks for.
builder_forms.change: Make the existing 'Audit' chip open a visible, immutable, exportable audit log capturing user, timestamp, and change detail for every edit and every AI-draft attestation, with Part-11-style e-signature metadata on the 'I have reviewed this AI draft' confirmation.

builder_forms.theme: No portfolio/rollup view for coordinators tracking many dossiers
builder_forms.quote: give me a portfolio-level dashboard - all dossiers, % complete, what's blocked, who owns it, target dates - and a client-ready export of that, because right now the visibility lives one dossier at a time behind an authoring UI.
builder_forms.change: Add a portfolio dashboard screen listing every dossier with % complete, outstanding sample/AI-draft flags, blocking items, assignee, and target/due date, with a client-ready CSV/PDF export — surfaced outside the single-dossier authoring UI.

builder_forms.theme: Per-client data siloing and AI data-residency unstated
builder_forms.quote: as a multi-client CDMO manager the whole walkthrough is single-dossier — no client/tenant separation, no evidence my sponsors' data stays siloed, and no word on where the AI drafting sends dossier facts. Until I see that, I couldn't put two competing clients' filings in the same tool.
builder_forms.change: Add an explicit per-client workspace boundary with a visible data-residency statement (where dossier data lives, whether it leaves Canada) and a plain note on the 'Draft with AI' toggle stating AI pre-fill runs only on that client's own facts with no cross-sponsor leakage.

builder_forms.theme: Scattered readiness signals; no single 'what's left before I can file' checklist
builder_forms.quote: right now the trust signals are scattered across the right rail, the document card, and the completeness card... give me a single dossier-level 'readiness manifest' I can export showing every section's state, provenance, and outstanding flags.
builder_forms.change: Add a one-click, printable/exportable dossier 'readiness manifest': a single plain-language checklist of every section's state, provenance, and outstanding sample/AI/bilingual flags, consolidating the right rail, banner, PM card, and completeness card into one view.

builder_forms.theme: Invented in-house jargon obscures plain regulatory meaning
builder_forms.quote: cut the cutesy jargon and say things plainly ('example text — you must replace this' instead of 'ghost'), and... a printable, plain checklist of what's still outstanding on a dossier.
builder_forms.change: Rename UI-invented terms in labels and tooltips to plain descriptions ('ghost'→'example text — replace this', 'eyebrow line'→section header, 'provenance chip'→source label, 'fingerprint md5'→document control ID).

ai_draft.theme: "Valid eCTD" gate is an unexplained binary — no eValidator-grade rule results
ai_draft.quote: real validation is a rule catalogue with errors, warnings, and pass/fail severities, and I'd want to see the actual eValidator-equivalent rule results, not a green checkmark
ai_draft.change: Make the "Valid eCTD" gate flag expandable into a rule-results panel that lists the specific eValidator/Health Canada profile rules checked with per-rule pass/fail/warning severity and the validation profile name + version, instead of a single green/red flag.

ai_draft.theme: Data-residency / AI-provider disclosure is buried and only asserted, not contractual
ai_draft.quote: I want to know exactly which provider and region the text goes to before I ever hit Send, not buried in a chip tooltip after saving — surface it at the mode toggle
ai_draft.change: Surface the named AI provider + region and the "isolated per sponsor, never used for training" statement inline at the "Draft with AI" mode toggle (before Send), with a link to the signed DPA, plus a per-sponsor toggle to disable AI drafting entirely for clients who forbid third-party LLMs.

ai_draft.theme: Guidance box shows a generic link, not the specific HC guidance version/date or inline text
ai_draft.quote: I'd want the guidance box to cite the specific Health Canada guidance version/date, not just a generic link
ai_draft.change: In the "What Health Canada needs here" box, resolve the guidance deep-link to the exact HC guidance document + section with its version/date shown, and render the relevant requirement text inline (expandable) so the required review can be done without leaving the page and the AI's draft can be checked clause-by-clause.

ai_draft.theme: No draft version history, in-app edit, or diff against the AI output
ai_draft.quote: let me diff or edit the AI draft before "Use this draft" rather than only accepting the latest reply wholesale
ai_draft.change: Add an in-app editor + version history on the document card so users can edit the AI draft before "Use this draft," see a diff of what they changed vs. what the AI wrote, and know whether "Use this draft" overwrites or preserves prior versions.

ai_draft.theme: Regulatory jargon (eCTD, gate flags, "fingerprint md5", attest) assumed, not explained
ai_draft.quote: put a one-line plain-English tooltip on every one. Also, "it knows what [section title] needs" is a literal unfilled placeholder in your copy
ai_draft.change: Add plain-language hover tooltips/glossary on every acronym and glyph (eCTD, req/opt, the three gate flags, "attest as your own content"), rename/de-emphasize "fingerprint md5" so it isn't mistaken for validation, and fix the literal unfilled "[section title]" placeholder in the guidance copy.

ai_draft.theme: Attestation is a self-checkbox — no second-reviewer/role gate and no visible audit record
ai_draft.quote: the attestation is a self-checkbox with no second-reviewer or role gate, and in a regulated shop I need a reviewer/approver separation, not the drafter attesting to their own work
ai_draft.change: Add an optional "flag for senior review" state between AI-draft and confirmed with a reviewer/approver role gate, surface the attestation's signer identity + timestamp + version visibly on the document card, and make the audit-trail entry inspectable/exportable (with tamper-evidence and what the reviewer changed).

ai_draft.theme: Bilingual / structured-XML content (French PM, label mock-ups) unaddressed
ai_draft.quote: address bilingualism head-on — say whether it drafts and reviews in French, because in Quebec that's non-negotiable
ai_draft.change: State explicitly at the "Draft with AI" mode whether it drafts/reviews bilingual (French) content and whether it produces the structured XML Product Monograph / label format, so labelling specialists know it's confined to narrative sections and never auto-fills regulated XML.

ai_draft.theme: No dossier-level roll-up of section status for PM reporting
ai_draft.quote: I need this rolled up across the whole dossier and across filings — how many sections are still "review & confirm," who owns each, what's blocking export — not just per-section chips
ai_draft.change: Add a dossier-level status roll-up view showing per-section draft/reviewed/confirmed/blocked state, the attester name, and what's blocking export across the whole submission, exportable for client status reports.

validate_export.theme: Validation profile version & Health Canada currency not on the card face
validate_export.quote: name the exact validation profile version and its Health Canada spec date on the card face, not buried in a toggle, because an out-of-date profile is worse than none
validate_export.change: On the Draft-completeness / validation card face (not inside a toggle), pin the exact validation profile name + version, the dated Health Canada eCTD validation-criteria release it mirrors, a 'last updated / effective date', and a changelog link; add per-report profile+version+timestamp+run-by provenance baked into the CSV/JSON header.

validate_export.theme: Screen density / 'construction-site' overload on one workspace
validate_export.quote: there's an awful lot crammed onto one screen — tabs, side rails, cards stacked on cards, chips everywhere. I'd need someone to sit with me the first few times before I stopped feeling lost
validate_export.change: Make the right-rail cards (Readiness, Draft completeness, Sequences, Technical check) collapsible/reorderable with the non-gating cards collapsed by default, and add a first-run guided walkthrough; surface a single primary 'what gates my export' focus so users aren't parsing four stacked cards at once.

validate_export.theme: eCTD jargon assumes knowledge — no glossary/primer for juniors, founders, newcomers, PMs, labelling
validate_export.quote: I'd want tooltips or a glossary link on 'leaf', 'sequence', 'lifecycle operators' and the purpose chips ... hovers vanish on a page
validate_export.change: Add an inline 'New to eCTD?' first-run primer plus a persistent glossary link defining leaf, sequence, working/active (0000/0001), and lifecycle operators (new/replace/delete) in one place — not hover-only, since hovers disappear on printouts and don't teach the concept.

validate_export.theme: Technical PDF/encryption check is vague and manual — should be specific and gate export by default
validate_export.quote: the 'Run technical check (PDF header/encryption)' being a separate manual button worries me; PDF encryption/version failures are a top rejection cause, so that should run by default, not on demand
validate_export.change: Fold the 'Run technical check' into the export gate so it runs automatically, and make it enumerate exactly what it inspects (PDF version, embedded fonts, encryption, bookmarks, hyperlinks, file/path length, byte limits) so 'technical check passed' isn't mistaken for eValidator-clean.

validate_export.theme: 'X% ready / filing steps' is an invented, ungrounded construct that risks false 'READY TO FILE' comfort
validate_export.quote: the invented 'X% ready' and 'filing steps' gamification, which is not a real regulatory construct and I'd have to mentally discard it
validate_export.change: On the Readiness card, cite each filing step's explicit regulatory basis (map step -> HC requirement) and visibly de-emphasize the '%' relative to the validation card, so a green 'READY TO FILE' can never be read as validation/cleared-to-file status; add a plain 'what still needs a human/external validator before you file' residual-risk statement near Export.

validate_export.theme: Error list truncation hides findings ('show first 5/8')
validate_export.quote: I'm wary that only the first 5 errors show by default — reviewers skim, and a hidden error is a missed deadline
validate_export.change: Show all findings by default (or make the full list one click, with filter-by-rule-id and by-module) in the export-blocked panel instead of 'show first 5/8, +X more'; provide one clean printable full-findings report with the profile name/version in the header for paper-based reviewers.

validate_export.theme: Audit trail & override need demonstrable tamper-evidence, attribution, and role gating
validate_export.quote: I'd want that override restricted by role and to trigger a countersignature, not just a free-text note
validate_export.change: On the override flow, capture named user + timestamp (not just a reason string), restrict override by role with a countersignature step, and surface the override event in a prominent non-editable, tamper-evident audit view stating who can see/edit it — so it survives a Part-11 inspector's first question.

validate_export.theme: No portfolio/cross-dossier rollup and no per-sponsor isolation for coordinators & CDMOs
validate_export.quote: give me a portfolio-level rollup ... right now everything lives inside one dossier workspace, so I can't see across dossiers who's blocked or what's due without opening each tile
validate_export.change: Add a portfolio-level view listing every dossier's blocked/ready state, its specific blocker, owner/assignee, target-filing-date and 'last checked' timestamp; stamp product/sponsor + sequence into each exported report filename and make cross-dossier isolation visibly obvious so one sponsor's sequence can never bleed into another's export.

validate_export.theme: No bilingual / French Module 1 completeness check for labelling
validate_export.quote: I'd add an explicit French/English pairing check for Module 1
validate_export.change: Add an explicit bilingual Module 1 completeness check (English/French product monograph, mock-ups, bilingual components present) and label on the Readiness card which steps are the labelling specialist's responsibility versus the publisher's.

operations.quote: a single dossier row is carrying module tower, gate chip, fee chip, litigation clock, collaboration chips and two links, and with 80 active dossiers on screen that becomes a wall of chips my analysts will have to squint at
operations.change: On the Portfolio dossier row, collapse to ONE primary status chip per dossier by default and move gate/fee/litigation/collaboration chips behind a per-row expand toggle, with a user-level 'chip density' preference (compact/detailed) that persists.

operations.theme: No filtering / saved views / personal queue
operations.quote: give me a way to collapse or configure the chip density per row and a saved filtered view (by client, by owner, by overdue) so my nine analysts aren't all scrolling the full portfolio
operations.change: Add a Portfolio filter/group bar (by client/sponsor, owner, overdue) plus a 'Just show my dossiers' toggle and saved-view persistence, so multi-sponsor CDMOs and junior staff can isolate their own rows.

operations.theme: Litigation clocks: no anchor-date override / source notice one click away
operations.quote: the 45-day action window and 24-month stay counters must let me see and override the anchor date, because I've seen HC-stamped receipt dates differ from what a tool infers, and a silently-wrong stay clock is a serious problem
operations.change: On each day-counter, add a 'View source notice' link that opens the underlying ingested document, plus an editable/override anchor-date field (with versioning when a hand-keyed anchor is corrected) and an explicit anchor timezone selector.

operations.theme: Multi-sponsor data isolation not stated in this flow
operations.quote: I need hard confirmation that 'your own workspace' means per-client data isolation — multi-sponsor confidentiality is non-negotiable and this walkthrough never says clients can't see each other's dossiers
operations.change: Add an explicit per-workspace data-isolation statement (and client-scoped visibility indicator) on the Portfolio/Registry flow confirming sponsors cannot see each other's dossiers.

operations.quote: give me a novice mode or an inline 'what does this deadline mean and what happens if I miss it' explainer, because right now the litigation and notice machinery assumes I already know Canadian drug-filing law
operations.change: Add a 'First ANDS / beginner mode' that hides the patent-litigation panels (Form V/NOA/s.6/stay) until enabled, and put an inline 'what this means / consequence if missed / whose clock it is' one-liner next to each correspondence counter, with glossary tooltips extended to every acronym (SAL/SDN/SRL/NOA/Form V), not just DIN/NOC/Right-to-Sell.

operations.theme: Exportable tamper-evident audit trail + self-documenting CSV
operations.quote: give me the audit trail as an exportable, tamper-evident record, not just an on-screen 'event stream,' and document who validated the day-counting rules
operations.change: Add an 'Export audit trail' action (tamper-evident, inspector-ready) alongside the status CSV, and include the counting basis and HC/PM(NOC) citation per due date in the CSV so the printed report stands alone.

operations.theme: 'Record only' non-transmit boundary needs to be even louder near actions/counters
operations.quote: the moment a director sees 'Serve NOA' or 'Ingest SAL' in a tool, they assume something was transmitted — I'd make the non-transmitting nature even harder to miss than a banner, perhaps a confirmation on each action
operations.change: Add a per-action confirmation ('This only records — nothing is sent to Health Canada') on Serve NOA / Ingest / Record s.6, and place the 'does not file' warning inline next to the day-counters, not just as a page banner.

operations.theme: Gate/module tower: real eCTD/eValidator status vs manual checklist unclear
operations.quote: a portfolio that shows 'Ready to file' without ever validating the actual eCTD backbone is a gate chip I can't fully trust on its own
operations.change: Label the gate chip / module tower to state whether it reflects real eCTD/eValidator/XML validation or a manual checklist, and clarify whether ingesting an SDN/SAL/SRL auto-updates gate status or is a pure log.

operations.theme: Bilingual / labelling artefacts absent from module tower
operations.quote: nothing here speaks to my actual job — French/English monograph content, mock-ups, XML PM structure — so I can't tell if bilingual labelling artefacts are handled at all, and for a Quebec manufacturer that's a gap
operations.change: Add explicit bilingual/PM module states (French & English monograph status, mock-up review, XML PM structure) to the module tower and confirm whether the interface itself is bilingual.

overall.quote: ship SAML/OIDC before you call yourself enterprise-ready ... per-workspace-only accounts and MFA won't clear enterprise IAM review indefinitely
overall.change: Add SAML/OIDC single sign-on as a first-class identity provider option in Workspace > Security settings (alongside the existing TOTP MFA), with a committed ship date shown on the roadmap card; until then surface the exact IdP/provisioning limitation inline on the login and account-provisioning screens.

overall.theme: Validation rule catalogue not versioned/traceable to HC guidance
overall.quote: publish the CA-E/CA-W rule catalogue with its source in HC guidance so I can audit it ... a stale rule set is worse than none
overall.change: On the Draft Completeness Check results screen add a 'Rule catalogue' panel that lists every CA-E-/CA-W- id mapped to its eCTD/eValidator criterion, with a visible ruleset version number and a 'Last aligned to Health Canada guidance on [date]' stamp; make the readiness percentage click through to the specific unmet rules behind it.

overall.theme: Bilingual / XML Product Monograph handling only asserted, never shown
overall.quote: show me the bilingual and XML Product Monograph handling in concrete detail, because that's my whole job and it's the one thing this overview waves past
overall.change: Add a dedicated Module 1 Product Monograph screen that shows the paired English/French monograph, validates the PM XML against Health Canada's current PM schema version (displayed on-screen), and flags PM-specific structural defects — not a single 'covered' claim.

overall.quote: 'cannot reach a filing unreviewed' is the right principle, but I need to see the enforcement, not just the sentence ... exactly who signs off and how that's recorded
overall.change: Add an explicit AI-draft review gate before export: show the named human reviewer, a required attestation checkbox with meaning ('I reviewed this machine-generated content'), timestamp, and record AI-draft provenance + the sign-off event in the append-only audit stream.

overall.theme: Portfolio/PM cross-dossier view buried, not first-class
overall.quote: the portfolio/PM layer — the whole reason I'd open this — is a throwaway clause at the end ... give me a real portfolio dashboard with deadlines, RAG status per dossier, and a client-shareable report
overall.change: Promote the portfolio layer to a top-level dashboard showing owner/client/deadline and RAG (who-is-blocked, next deadline) per dossier as a top-level chip, with a client-facing status export and Smartsheet/MS Project export/integration.

overall.quote: so a nervous junior like me doesn't over-trust the '34% ready' chip and think green means done ... define exactly what '34% ready' means
overall.change: On the readiness chip add a persistent hover/label defining it as 'format & presence completeness only — NOT filing-ready; run eValidator + human review', and surface the 'NOT Health Canada review' disclaimer on the hero/landing page rather than only inside the validation screen.

overall.theme: 3D 'submission tower' is decoration; want plain checklist default
overall.quote: drop or heavily de-emphasize the 3D 'submission tower' — it's decoration and I don't trust decoration on a regulatory tool; make the plain checklist the default
overall.change: Make the plain checklist the default module-status view and demote the 3D submission tower to an opt-in toggle, with a per-user preference to permanently dismiss the 3D view and plain-language tooltips for expert users.
